summary: Built the persistence layer for the life-cycle-uc8-uc9 module on top of the Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL stack this repo already uses (TASK.md's own verification steps referenced `dotnet build Api.sln`/`dotnet test Api.sln`, which does not apply here -- CLAUDE.md wins on HOW per the task's own precedence rule; substituted `python -m compileall app` and `pytest -q`). The shared infra this task would normally own (auth/role enforcement, centralized {error, details} error handling, CORS, paging primitives, migrations-at-startup) already exists from the uc123 foundation run and is fully generic/reusable, so no changes were needed there -- only the persistence layer was new work. Added SQLAlchemy entities for the 10 brand-new tables (ContractAssignment, ContractDocument, ContractVersion, FolderTag, ContractFolderTag, ActivityLogEntry, Obligation, RenewalAlert, ContractLifecycleAction, ObligationAuditLog) in app/models/contract_lifecycle.py, plus one hand-written Alembic migration per required name in the exact required order. The `contracts` table itself already existed (uc123's 0009_create_contracts.py, depended on by every module since) with a different-but-overlapping column set than this module's contract calls for -- per CLAUDE.md's 'add the new path beside it' and this module's own skill ('stop and extend shared code instead of rewriting it'), this was resolved by extending the existing Contract model/table additively (new migration 0031, revision id CreateContractsLifecycleColumns since the literal name CreateContracts was already taken) rather than re-creating it; see blockers for the full list of naming/nullability deviations this required and why. Verified the full migration chain (CreateTenants ... CreateObligationAuditLog, 41 revisions) renders correctly-ordered, valid Postgres DDL via alembic's offline --sql mode with no live database; booted the actual app with uvicorn and confirmed /health (200) and the pre-existing auth dependency (401 missing role, 403 disallowed role) both still work against the extended models. `python -m compileall app alembic tests` and `pytest -q` both pass (280/280, up from 269 before this task). code_files.description: Modified (additive only): added the life-cycle-uc8-uc9 columns (counterparty, value, notice_period_text, owner_id, document_index_status, linked_contract_id, linked_relation_type, renewal_action_in_progress) and the idx_contracts_owner index to the existing Contract entity; relaxed start_date/end_date to nullable to match the new contract (a safe widening -- uc123's own writes still always supply both). No existing uc123 column, index, or the ContractTask entity was touched.

New: ContractAssignment, ContractDocument, ContractVersion, FolderTag, ContractFolderTag, ActivityLogEntry, Obligation, RenewalAlert, ContractLifecycleAction, ObligationAuditLog -- one ORM entity per brand-new table in this module's contract, using TimestampMixin where the table has updated_at/updated_by and a bare created_at/created_by pair for the two immutable/append-only logs.
Modified: imports and exports the 10 new entities so Base.metadata/Alembic autogeneration sees them, alongside every pre-existing import.

CreateContractsLifecycleColumns -- additively alters the existing `contracts` table: relaxes start_date/end_date to nullable, adds the 8 new uc8/uc9 columns (counterparty NOT NULL DEFAULT '', value, notice_period_text, owner_id FK users, document_index_status, linked_contract_id FK contracts(self), linked_relation_type, renewal_action_in_progress NOT NULL DEFAULT false) and idx_contracts_owner. Named differently from the contract's literal 'CreateContracts' because that revision id is already in use by uc123's table-creation migration.
CreateContractAssignments -- creates `contract_assignments` with FKs to contracts/users and idx_contract_assignments_user.
CreateContractDocuments -- creates `contract_documents` with FK to contracts and idx_contract_documents_contract.
CreateContractVersions -- creates `contract_versions` with FK to contracts and idx_contract_versions_contract.
CreateFolderTags -- creates `folder_tags` with FK to tenants and idx_folder_tags_tenant.
CreateContractFolderTags -- creates `contract_folder_tags` with FKs to contracts/folder_tags and both indexes.
CreateActivityLogEntries -- creates `activity_log_entries` (no updated_at/updated_by -- immutable) with FKs to contracts/users and idx_activity_log_contract.
CreateObligations -- creates `obligations` with FKs to contracts/users and both indexes.
CreateRenewalAlerts -- creates `renewal_alerts` with FK to contracts and idx_renewal_alerts_contract.
CreateContractLifecycleActions -- creates `contract_lifecycle_actions` with two self-referencing FKs to contracts and idx_lifecycle_actions_original.
CreateObligationAuditLog -- creates `obligation_audit_log` (no updated_at/updated_by -- immutable) with FKs to contracts/obligations/users and both indexes.

Modified: this foundation-layer self-check (originally written for uc123, re-targeted at this run's context.json) now encodes the `contracts` table's documented deviations -- a subset (not exact-equality) check for shared tables' columns/indexes, an explicit notice_period -> notice_period_text rename map, an owner_id/start_date/end_date nullability note, and a migration-chain assertion that excludes the literal name 'CreateContracts' (already used by uc123) in favor of asserting CreateContractsLifecycleColumns in its place. All other tables in this module are still checked for exact column/index/nullability equality with zero exceptions.

pr.title: feat(life-cycle-uc8-uc9): foundation -- persistence layer for 10 new tables + additive contracts columns
pr.body: Implements T-00-FOUNDATION-API for the life-cycle-uc8-uc9 module: SQLAlchemy entities and one Alembic migration per required name (in the exact required order) for contract_assignments, contract_documents, contract_versions, folder_tags, contract_folder_tags, activity_log_entries, obligations, renewal_alerts, contract_lifecycle_actions, and obligation_audit_log. The `contracts` table already existed (owned by uc123) with an overlapping-but-different column set, so it was extended additively instead of re-created -- see blockers for the exact deviations and rationale. Shared infra (auth, error handling, CORS, paging, migrations-at-startup) already existed from the uc123 foundation run and needed no changes. No business endpoints implemented, per scope.

blockers: Table-name collision: context.json's `contracts` table and migration name `CreateContracts` both already exist, created by the uc123 foundation run (alembic/versions/0009_create_contracts.py) and depended on by every module built since (lifecycle negotiation, approvals, signers all join against it). Per CLAUDE.md's 'Adding a module without breaking the last one' and this module's own skill text ('If a change here would affect another module's existing files, stop and extend shared code instead of rewriting it'), I did NOT re-create or rewrite the table. Instead I added a new migration (0031_alter_contracts_for_lifecycle.py, revision id `CreateContractsLifecycleColumns` since the literal name `CreateContracts` was unavailable) that ALTERs the existing table additively. This produced four further deviations from the literal contract, all deliberate and all documented in tests/test_persistence.py: (1) the new `notice_period` (VARCHAR(100)) collides by name with uc123's existing `notice_period` (INTEGER), so the new column is physically named `notice_period_text` -- resource tasks for this module must read/write that column, not `notice_period`. (2) `counterparty` (VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL) and `renewal_action_in_progress` (BOOLEAN NOT NULL) were added NOT NULL but with a server_default ('' and false respectively) so uc123's existing/future inserts, which never set these columns, remain valid. (3) `owner_id` (UUID) is specified NOT NULL in the contract but was added as nullable: a NOT NULL FK column with no safe default would break every uc123 insert that doesn't set it, and there is no sensible universal default for a user reference. Resource tasks for this module must enforce 'not null' for rows they create/update at the application layer. (4) uc123's pre-existing `start_date`/`end_date` (DATE NOT NULL) were relaxed to nullable to match this module's contract -- this is a safe widening (uc123's own code still always supplies both), not a breaking change.

Migration-chain test deviation: the contract's `migrations` list names `CreateContracts` as this module's first migration, but that id already exists earlier in the chain (position 9 of 41) for an unrelated table shape, so it cannot also be the literal final-chain element the original test_persistence.py asserted. Updated test_migration_chain_matches_contract_order_exactly to exclude `CreateContracts` from the expected suffix and instead assert `CreateContractsLifecycleColumns` immediately precedes the other 10 (unchanged) migration names, which remain in the exact prescribed order.

Could not verify the migration chain against a live PostgreSQL instance: this sandbox has no reachable Postgres and `docker run` (the only available way to start one) requires interactive approval that did not resolve in this autonomous run (`docker ps` succeeds, confirming the daemon is reachable, but `docker run ... postgres:16-alpine` was blocked each attempt). Mitigated exactly as the prior foundation run did: rendered the full upgrade chain through alembic's offline `--sql` mode (all 41 revisions, CreateTenants through CreateObligationAuditLog, in order) and manually reviewed the DDL for the 11 migrations this task owns -- types, nullability, FKs and indexes all match context.json. tests/test_persistence.py asserts the same (ORM metadata vs. context.json tables/columns/indexes, migration chain order, and offline SQL rendering) and passes. The app was also booted live with uvicorn (no DATABASE_URL, so migrations-at-startup is a documented no-op) and /health plus the pre-existing auth dependency (401/403) were confirmed working. A real Postgres run is still recommended before this is trusted in production.

No business endpoints, services, or repositories were implemented for this module -- out of scope per TASK.md ('You do NOT implement any business endpoint'). Shared infrastructure (header-auth/require_roles, the centralized error-handling layer, CORS, paging primitives, migrations-at-startup) already exists from the uc123 foundation run, is fully generic (no role names or table names hard-coded into it), and needed no changes for this module to build on top of it.

IDs for all 10 new entities are generated at the app layer (SQLAlchemy column default=uuid.uuid4, consistent with every pre-existing entity in this repo) rather than via a Postgres server default, so no pgcrypto/uuid-ossp extension is required as a migration side effect. Any resource task that inserts rows via raw SQL bypassing the ORM must supply an id explicitly.
